findings.topic: Why the router picks nftables and why the observed error appears
findings.what: Up() -> setNetfilterModeLocked(netfilterOff) -> setupNetfilterLocked(kind="") -> linuxfw.New(logf, "") -> detectFirewallMode. With no TS_DEBUG_FIREWALL_MODE and an empty pref hint, the iptables probe is skipped because buildfeatures.HasIPTables is false under ts_omit_iptables, and the function falls through to `logf("default choosing nftables")` (the exact log line seen). Even a c2n/nodeattr hint of "auto" returns nftables immediately when !HasIPTables. Then the first real Set(cfg) with NetfilterMode=on (prefs default) calls nfr.AddChains(): each table/chain is flushed to the kernel individually, so filter table + FORWARD/INPUT (type filter) succeed, then the nat table succeeds, then the POSTROUTING chain of ChainTypeNAT fails with `create postrouting chain: add chain: conn.Receive: netlink receive: no such file or directory`. ENOENT here is the kernel's nf_tables_chain_type_lookup returning ERR_PTR(-ENOENT) because the "nat" chain type (nft_chain_nat) is not registered on the WSA kernel. Upstream's own detector describes this exact error string as 'partial nftables support' and would have caught it with createDummyPostroutingChains -- but that code only runs in "auto" mode with iptables compiled in, never in this build.

findings.topic: Why table 52 is empty and no 52xx rules exist (most likely cause) and where the exit-node route actually went
findings.what: Rules are only added when r.ipRuleAvailable, which is set once at construction from netlink.RuleList(FAMILY_V4); on failure the router logs `error querying IP rules (does kernel have IP_MULTIPLE_TABLES?)` and `warning: running without policy routing`. With ipRuleAvailable=false, addIPRules/delIPRules are no-ops, throw routes are skipped, and routeTable() returns 0, which tailscale/netlink encodes as RT_TABLE_MAIN. So 0.0.0.0/0 dev tailscale0, ::/0 and every peer /32 are written into Android's MAIN table -- a table no Android rule ever consults (netd flushes every rule except priority 0 at init, including the kernel's 32766/32767 main/default rules, and never populates RT_TABLE_MAIN; its per-network tables are ifindex+1000). The observed Set() error names only the netfilter step, which is consistent with the route adds having succeeded somewhere. Note Set() continues past the netfilter error (errors are joined), so routes/addresses are still attempted.

It also means the netfilter/nftables error is a red herring for the routing symptom: fixing the firewall runner alone would leave the exit node exactly as broken.

findings.topic: Upstream ip-rule design (5210/5230/5250/5270) is structurally incompatible with Android, regardless of iptables vs nftables
findings.what: baseIPRules at base 5200: 5210 `fwmark 0x80000/0xff0000 lookup main`, 5230 `... lookup default`, 5250 `... unreachable`, 5270 `from all lookup 52`. Two Android facts break it: (a) main and default are EMPTY on Android (netd keeps physical default routes in tables ifindex+1000 and deleted the 32766/32767 rules), so any packet carrying the bypass mark falls to 5250 and is UNREACHABLE; (b) the Android netns build never sets the bypass mark: netns_android.go UseSocketMark() returns false and controlC only calls androidProtectFunc/androidBindToNetworkFunc, both of which are set by the official Android app via JNI and are registered by nothing in this tree. So the daemon's DERP, control, STUN and disco sockets are UNmarked and match 5270 `from all lookup 52` -- at priority 5270, ahead of every netd rule (10000-32000). The moment table 52 holds 0.0.0.0/0 dev tailscale0 (i.e. the exit node route is installed correctly), tailscaled's own tunnel traffic is routed into tailscale0: a routing loop and total loss of connectivity. The UBNT variant (single inverted rule `not fwmark 0x80000/0xff0000 lookup 52`) would avoid the unreachable trap but still needs a marked daemon.

findings.topic: Tailscale's fwmark bits collide with Android's Fwmark layout
findings.what: Android packs its routing decision into the fwmark: netId bits 0-15, explicitlySelected bit 16 (0x10000), protectedFromVpn bit 17 (0x20000), permission bits 18-19 (PERMISSION_NETWORK=0x1 -> 0x40000, PERMISSION_SYSTEM=0x3 -> 0xC0000), uidBillingDone bit 20 (0x100000). Tailscale's subnet mark 0x40000 IS Android's PERMISSION_NETWORK bit, its bypass mark 0x80000 is the upper permission bit, and its mask 0xff0000 covers all five Android flag bits. Concretely: ts-forward `-i tailscale0 -j MARK --set-mark 0x40000/0xff0000` would stamp forwarded packets with PERMISSION_NETWORK and clear explicit/protected bits; the connmark rp_filter workaround (`CONNMARK --restore-mark --nfmask 0xff0000 --ctmask 0xff0000` in mangle PREROUTING, plus sysctl src_valid_mark=1) rewrites those Android bits on inbound packets; netd's own `mangle INPUT -j MARK --set-mark <fwmark>/0xffefffff` (modifyIncomingPacketMark) in turn clobbers Tailscale's bits; and Android's init.rc sets tcp_fwmark_accept=1 and fwmark_reflect=1, so such marks propagate into accepted sockets and reflected packets. Android rules that match permission use `mask.permission = permission` (modifyExplicitNetworkRule, modifyOutputInterfaceRules, modifyVpnSystemPermissionRule), so a 0x40000-marked packet satisfies PERMISSION_NETWORK checks. The app already avoided all of this by using bit 24 through a mask (RootUtils.kt).

Whatever routes the tunnel must use a mark bit above bit 20; the app's 0x1000000 is a correct choice and a daemon bypass mark should be another high bit (e.g. 0x2000000), never 0x80000.

findings.topic: Reply-path (rp_filter) caveat for the recommended rule
findings.what: With `not fwmark BYPASS lookup 1099` and a default route in 1099, replies to the daemon's marked sockets arrive on wlan0 and are reverse-path-checked with mark 0 (unless src_valid_mark=1), which would resolve to tailscale0 and be dropped as martians IF rp_filter is strict (1). Upstream solves this on desktop with connmark save/restore + src_valid_mark=1. Android's init.rc does not set rp_filter (only fwmark_reflect and tcp_fwmark_accept), so the kernel default (0) likely applies, but vendor kernels/WSA may differ. Also note the DNS forwarder's UDP sockets use stdNetPacketListener (not the netns hook) when no link selector is installed, so its upstream queries would follow the exit-node default route -- acceptable (no DNS leak) but worth knowing.
findings.evidence: SRC/wgengine/router/osrouter/router_linux.go:550-575 (why upstream needs connmark + src_valid_mark). Android system/core/rootdir/init.rc (android13-release): only fwmark_reflect=1 and tcp_fwmark_accept=1, no rp_filter/src_valid_mark writes. findings.topic: DNS with an exit node (secondary to the router, but relevant to 'nothing loads')
findings.what: When an exit node is selected and the exit node peer has Cap>=26 (or a PeerAPIDNS service), dnsConfigForNetmap replaces the default resolvers with the exit node's DoH endpoint (http://<exit-ip>:<peerapi-port>/dns-query) and returns early; DNS then rides the tailnet (reachable today via the app's 100.64/10 rules). If the exit node cannot proxy DNS (older node, or WireGuard-only without ExitNodeDNSResolvers), DefaultResolvers stays empty, only nm.DNS.FallbackResolvers (usually none) are added -- matching the observed `DefaultResolvers:[]` with split-domain Routes. The DNS manager then, because the noop configurator has SupportsSplitDNS()=false, points the OS at 100.100.100.100 and blends the base config; patch 11 makes noop GetBaseConfig return TS_DNS_FALLBACK (1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8), so the forwarder still has upstreams. findings.topic: netd's fwmark layout and whether 0x80000 is tolerated
findings.what: AOSP system/netd Fwmark.h (recollection, verify with `ip rule` on device): bits 0-15 netId, bit 16 explicitlySelected, bit 17 protectedFromVpn, bits 18-19 permission (PERMISSION_NETWORK = bit 18, PERMISSION_SYSTEM = bits 18+19), bit 20 uidBillingDone; bits 21-31 unused. 0x80000 is bit 19 alone — an encoding netd never produces. netd's rules only mask the permission bits when the target network requires a permission (NETWORK: mask bit 18; SYSTEM: mask bits 18+19), so bit 19 alone never satisfies them; the default-network rule is `from all fwmark 0x0/0xffff lookup <iface>` (netId 0, permission unmasked) and still matches. Hence a socket whose mark is exactly 0x80000 is routed by netd exactly like an unmarked one, cannot accidentally use a restricted network, and does not collide with the app's bit 24 (RootUtils.kt:32-33) or with Tailscale's own mask 0xff0000 (5210 needs bits 16-23 == 0x08, satisfied). Since the daemon's Go sockets have mark 0 today (raw syscalls, no libnetd_client), SO_MARK=0x80000 loses nothing. Caveat: netd-marked sockets of system-permission apps (uid 1000 system_server, networkstack, netd's own resolver which uses netId|explicit|PERMISSION_SYSTEM = 0xD00xx) also have bit 19 set — an app rule keyed on 'bit 19 set/clear' therefore also lets those bypass the exit node; a stricter `fwmark 0x80000/0xff0000` match (exactly Tailscale's pattern) excludes them because they carry bits 16 and 18 as well.
findings.evidence: External: AOSP system/netd/include/Fwmark.h and server/RouteController.cpp (modifyDefaultNetworkRule, modifyExplicitNetworkRule, modifyVpnUidRangeRule with IIF_LOOPBACK); repo: /home/pinus/projects/tailsocks/app/src/main/java/io/github/bropines/tailscaled/core/RootUtils.kt:22-33; /home/pinus/projects/tailsocks/appctr/tailscale_src/tsconst/linuxfw.go:31-42

For the app's bypass rule prefer the exact match `fwmark 0x80000/0xff0000` (only the daemon) over `0x80000/0x80000` (daemon + system-permission traffic); for a negative catch-all rule, `fwmark 0x0/0x80000` unavoidably exempts system-permission traffic too — acceptable (connectivity checks stay on the physical path) but must be a conscious choice.

findings.topic: Source-address selection: why iptables owner-marking cannot replace SO_MARK/uidrange
findings.what: For locally generated packets the kernel does the first route lookup at connect()/sendmsg() with the socket's sk_mark and uid and picks the source address from that result; a mangle OUTPUT `MARK` only triggers a re-route (`ip_route_me_harder`) that keeps the already chosen source. RootUtils.kt:376-382 already documents this for the reverse case (root-owned DNS forwarder socket leaving tailscale0 with the Wi-Fi source), which is why the `to 100.64.0.0/10` rule exists. So `iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT -m owner --uid-owner 0 -j MARK …` would make the daemon's exit-node-bypassed packets leave wlan0 with a 100.x source. Only SO_MARK (sk_mark, seen by the first lookup) or a fib rule on `uidrange` (flowi4_uid is the socket uid at the first lookup) are correct primitives. uidrange caveats: (1) forwarded and kernel-originated lookups carry uid 0 (`sock_net_uid(net, NULL)`), so netd always pairs uid rules with `iif lo` (IIF_LOOPBACK) — the app must do the same; (2) toybox/busybox `ip rule` do not support `uidrange`, and github.com/tailscale/netlink's Rule has no UIDRange field (`go doc github.com/tailscale/netlink.Rule`), so neither the su shell nor the vendored netlink can install it without extra tooling; (3) uid 0 also covers netd's resolver (DNS queries that escape the TAILSOCKS_DNS DNAT, i.e. those to the bypass resolvers 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 at RootUtils.kt:414-417, would leak past the exit node) and every root shell/Magisk/KernelSU module.

findings.topic: Exact app-managed rule set (Option A): what to install when an exit node is active and remove when not
findings.what: Preconditions: SO_MARK patch (daemon sockets carry 0x80000); the existing pref-100 rules and table-1099 /10 routes stay. INSTALL (run via su, IPv4 then IPv6): (1) find the physical default table: `PHYS=$(ip rule show | sed -n 's/.*fwmark 0x0\/0xffff lookup \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n1)` (netd's DEFAULT_NETWORK rule, prints the table name e.g. wlan0/rmnet_data0 or a number); if not numeric, `PHYS_T=$((1000 + $(cat /sys/class/net/$PHYS/ifindex)))` (netd table = ifindex+1000; names live in /data/misc/net/rt_tables which busybox ip cannot resolve); same with `ip -6 rule show` for PHYS6_T; verify `ip route show table $PHYS_T | grep -q '^default'`. (2) daemon bypass, before the daemon's 5210 and before the catch-all: `ip rule add fwmark 0x80000/0xff0000 iif lo lookup $PHYS_T pref 150`; `ip -6 rule add fwmark 0x80000/0xff0000 iif lo lookup $PHYS6_T pref 150`. (3) exit-node routes in 1099: `ip route replace default dev tailscale0 table 1099 metric 1`; `ip -6 route replace default dev tailscale0 table 1099 metric 1` if tailscale0 has an fd7a address, else `ip -6 route replace unreachable default table 1099` (no v6 leak, mirrors local.go:6541-6565 intent); safety throws: `ip route replace throw 169.254.0.0/16 table 1099`, `throw 224.0.0.0/4`, `throw 255.255.255.255/32`, `ip -6 route replace throw fe80::/10 table 1099`, `throw ff00::/8`. (4) only if prefs.ExitNodeAllowLANAccess: one `ip route replace throw <net>/<len> table 1099` per on-link prefix of every UP non-tailscale0 interface (`ip -o -4 addr show scope global up`, network-masked), same for `-6` (equivalent of router_linux.go addThrowRoute for LocalRoutes). (5) catch-all: `ip rule add fwmark 0x0/0x80000 iif lo lookup 1099 pref 200`; `ip -6 rule add fwmark 0x0/0x80000 iif lo lookup 1099 pref 200`. (6) if `/proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter` or `conf/$PHYS/rp_filter` is 1, set 2 (remember old value) — see rp_filter finding. (7) verify: `ip rule show` contains `150:` and `200:.*fwmark 0x0/0x80000` (mask printed → the ip binary emitted FRA_FWMASK; a bare `fwmark 0x0` would match everything) and `ip route show table 1099 | grep -q '^default dev tailscale0'`. Ordering: 0 local < 100 (app tailnet rules) < 150 (daemon bypass) < 200 (catch-all) < 5210-5270 (daemon, now inert for local traffic) < 10000-32000 (netd) < 32766 main. design.root_cause:
Patch 13 (appctr/patches/13-android-osrouter.patch:7-8) compiles the desktop-Linux router wgengine/router/osrouter/router_linux.go on Android unchanged; every assumption that router makes is false in Root Mode.

(1) Netfilter (the logged error). Prefs default NetfilterMode=on (ipn/prefs.go:749 -> router.Config at ipn/ipnlocal/local.go:6530). appctr/build.sh:90 passes ts_omit_iptables, so linuxfw.detectFirewallMode cannot probe iptables and logs 'default choosing nftables' (util/linuxfw/detector.go:45-75; linuxfw.New at util/linuxfw/nftables_runner.go:635-661). The first Set() with mode=on runs setNetfilterModeLocked -> nfr.AddChains() (router_linux.go:461, 823-835), which fails on WSA at the nat POSTROUTING chain because that kernel lacks the nft 'nat' chain type ('create postrouting chain: add chain: ... no such file or directory', nftables_runner.go:962-974). Set() joins the error and continues (router_linux.go:444-475); wgengine records it via SetRouterHealth (wgengine/userspace.go:895-901) -> the persistent 'router' warning and the 'router config failed' line on every reconfig. Even on a kernel where nft works (Redmi), Tailscale's marks 0x40000/0x80000 mask 0xff0000 (tsconst/linuxfw.go:31-42) are netd's Fwmark permission bits (bits 18-19) and the router would insert CGNAT DROP, connmark and jump rules into netd-owned INPUT/FORWARD/POSTROUTING.

(2) Policy routing (why the exit node cannot work). The router installs 5210 'fwmark 0x80000/0xff0000 lookup main', 5230 '... lookup default', 5250 '... unreachable', 5270 'from all lookup 52' (router_linux.go:141, 1594-1628, 1659-1691) and writes every route, including 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 added for an exit node (local.go:6547-6565), into table 52 (router_linux.go:1190-1206; routeTable() 1375-1380 returns 52 only if ipRuleAvailable, else 0 = RT_TABLE_MAIN). On Android main/default are empty (netd flushes all rules except pref 0 at init and keeps physical routes in per-interface tables ifindex+1000). Decisive: the Android netns build never marks the daemon's sockets — net/netns/netns_android.go:25-28 UseSocketMark() returns false, controlC (:72-108) only calls androidProtectFunc/androidBindToNetworkFunc, which nothing in this tree registers; the SO_MARK code lives in netns_linux.go (:4 tag 'linux && !android', :113-118) and is excluded. So with an exit node either (a) the 52xx rules exist and 5270 sends tailscaled's own WireGuard/DERP/control packets into tailscale0 -> routing loop -> nothing loads (matches the symptom), or (b) the RuleList probe failed (router_linux.go:157-167), ipRuleAvailable=false, routes landed in RT_TABLE_MAIN which no Android rule consults -> the exit node is silently inert. Both are broken. Which one WSA is in has never actually been observed: the app's Check Routing screen filters everything by '1099' (RootUtils.kt:511-516), so 52xx rules and table 52 were invisible there — verification step 0 settles it.

(3) DNS is secondary. With an exit node that cannot proxy DNS, DefaultResolvers is empty (ipn/ipnlocal/node_backend.go:1599-1616) and the '.' route comes from TS_DNS_FALLBACK (patch 11, net/dns/noop.go); the forwarder's UDP upstream socket is unmarked (net/dns/resolver/forwarder.go:504-512), so DNS works today and will ride the exit node after the fix. appctr's OverrideDNSResolvers field (appctr/appctr.go:385-412) does not exist in ipn.MaskedPrefs and is silently ignored by LocalAPI (ipn/localapi/localapi.go:1010-1011).
design.recommendation:
Keep the app as the owner of ip rules and netfilter on Android. Make the daemon (a) mark its own sockets and (b) stop installing desktop rules and netfilter, keeping only what only it knows: addresses, and routes into table 52 (peer /32s, accepted subnet routes, 100.100.100.100/32, 'default dev tailscale0' when an exit node is set, RTN_THROW for LAN prefixes when allow-lan-access is on). The app adds ONE permanent rule that is safe with or without an exit node:

  200: from all iif lo fwmark 0x0/0x2000000 lookup 52

Unmarked, locally generated traffic consults the daemon's table first (no match -> falls through to netd exactly as today; default route -> tailscale0 when an exit node is active; throw -> netd for LAN when allowed). tailscaled's sockets carry SO_MARK 0x2000000 (bit 25: outside Android's Fwmark bits 0-20, distinct from the app's bit 24, low 16 bits 0 so netd's 'fwmark 0x0/0xffff lookup <default>' still matches it) and therefore skip the rule and reach the physical network through netd's own 10000+ rules. No physical-table discovery, no Wi-Fi/cellular handover re-apply, no exit-node state machine in Kotlin: toggling the exit node is handled by router.Set() as on desktop Linux.

Final rule order: 0 local | 100 app 'fwmark 0x1000000/0x1000000 lookup 1099' and 'to 100.64.0.0/10 lookup 1099' (existing, unchanged; v6 fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48) | 200 app catch-all -> 52 (new) | 5200-5299 daemon: nothing (stale rules purged) | 10000-32000 netd | 32766/32767 main/default (deleted by netd, irrelevant). Netfilter is forced off in the daemon on android, so the nft error and the 'router' health warning disappear; the app's TAILSOCKS_MARK/TAILSOCKS_DNS/FORWARD rules stay as they are.

Bypass evidence for this build: netns.Listener/NewDialer/FromDialer attach control() to every daemon socket (net/netns/netns.go:90-130): magicsock UDP (wgengine/magicsock/magicsock.go:3712, 4082), DERP (derp/derphttp/derphttp_client.go:612,714), control plane via tsdial.SystemDial (net/tsdial/tsdial.go:538-541), netcheck/STUN (net/netcheck/netcheck.go:895,1201), dnsfallback (net/dnsfallback/dnsfallback.go:136). Today that hook is a no-op on android; adding the same unix.SetsockoptInt(SOL_SOCKET, SO_MARK) that netns_linux.go:113-118 uses makes it effective, and root under Magisk/KernelSU/APatch has CAP_NET_ADMIN. The kernel side is exactly netd's own idiom (fib rule match is (rule.mark ^ skb.mark) & mask; FRA_FWMARK=0 + FRA_FWMASK=0x2000000 matches only unmarked-bit-25 packets; iif lo = output lookups only). Runtime proof is verification step 3 (a mangle counter on --mark 0x2000000/0x2000000 rising while connected) and step 5 ('ip route get 8.8.8.8 mark 0x2000000' resolving to wlan0 while 'ip route get 8.8.8.8' resolves to tailscale0).

Rejected alternatives: building with iptables (fixes only the health warning, keeps the loop and writes netd's mark bits); TS_DEBUG_FIREWALL_MODE=iptables on this binary (hard start failure: util/linuxfw/iptables_disabled.go:14-20 -> router.Up error -> tailscaled.go exits); router.NewFake (no link-up, no addresses, Kotlin would have to re-derive netmap routes); uidrange fib rules (uid 0 covers every root process and still needs the dynamic physical table); the 'not fwmark' inverted rule (FIB_RULE_INVERT negates the whole match including iif lo, so forwarded packets would be captured).
rules_v4: # All of these are PERMANENT: installed together with the existing table-1099 block in RootUtils.applyTailscale0Routing (RootUtils.kt:373-391) and in tailscaled.sh (:116-131). Nothing is exit-node-conditional; the daemon's router.Set() adds/removes 'default dev tailscale0' in table 52 by itself. Existing lines (ip route replace 100.64.0.0/10 dev tailscale0 table 1099 metric 1; the two priority-100 rules; TAILSOCKS_MARK; TAILSOCKS_DNS; FORWARD ACCEPT) stay exactly as they are.

# 1. Purge the desktop-Linux rules a pre-fix core left behind (a killed daemon never ran Close(); a stale '5270: from all lookup 52' would swallow the new daemon's marked packets). With the new core nothing re-adds them; an old core re-adds them within ~5 s (onIPRuleDeleted), harmless.
for p in 5210 5230 5250 5270; do while ip rule del pref $p 2>/dev/null; do :; done; done

# 2. Catch-all: unmarked, locally generated traffic consults the daemon's table 52 first (peer /32s, subnet routes, exit-node default, LAN throws); anything else falls through to netd. 'iif lo' = output route lookups only, so forwarded/tethered packets stay on netd's rules.
ip rule del fwmark 0x0/0x2000000 iif lo lookup 52 2>/dev/null || true
ip rule add fwmark 0x0/0x2000000 iif lo lookup 52 priority 200

# 3. Verify the mask really landed. A rule that reads back as bare 'fwmark 0x0' has mask 0 in the kernel and matches EVERY packet, daemon included (= loop). Delete it if so; non-fatal for the rest of the script, but the marker line must be logged by RootUtils.
ip rule show | grep -q '^200:.*fwmark 0x0/0x2000000.*lookup 52' || { while ip rule del priority 200 lookup 52 2>/dev/null; do :; done; echo 'verify: ip binary dropped the fwmark mask; exit-node catch-all NOT installed'; }

# 4. Reverse-path filter: replies to the daemon's marked sockets arriving on wlan0 are rp_filter-checked with mark 0 and iif lo, resolve to tailscale0 through table 52 and are dropped as martians under strict mode (1). Loose (2) accepts them. Effective value is max(all, iface), so raising 'all' to 2 is sufficient. Remember the original for cleanup.
for f in /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/*/rp_filter; do [ "$(cat "$f")" = "1" ] && { [ -f /data/adb/tailsocks/rp_filter.orig ] || cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter > /data/adb/tailsocks/rp_filter.orig; echo 2 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter; break; }; done

# 5. NO route commands for table 52. It is written by the daemon (router_linux.go: RouteReplace of cfg.Routes at 1190-1206, RTN_THROW for cfg.LocalRoutes at 1212-1231). The app must never flush, add to, or verify-fail on table 52; the 1099 blanket routes stay.

cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/wlan0/rp_filter 2>/dev/null   # after apply: all=2 if any interface was 1

# 9. exit node off again
$TS set --exit-node=; sleep 3; ip route show table 52 | grep -c '^default'   # 0
ip route get 8.8.8.8   # wlan0 again ; ip route get <peer-tailnet-ip> still dev tailscale0

# 10. cleanup path (Root Mode off / Stop with kill): ip rule show has no 100/200 rules; ip route show table 1099 is empty; table 52 empties by itself once tailscale0 is gone; rp_filter restored if it was changed
# 11. Redmi (Android 16): repeat 1-9; in addition `ip -6 rule show | grep 200:` and `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/*/rp_filter | sort -u`, and confirm no vendor daemon re-adds rules below 200
risks: Strict rp_filter (1) on 'all' or the physical interface drops inbound WireGuard/DERP replies as martians once the pref-200 rule exists (the kernel's reverse lookup runs with iif lo and mark 0, hits table 52 -> tailscale0 != wlan0). Mitigated by the rp_filter=2 step (verify step 8). Upstream solves the same problem with connmark + src_valid_mark, which needs netfilter on and is deliberately not used here.

IPv6 leak: if the daemon judges IPv6 unusable (CheckIPv6 fails or /proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/tailscale0/disable_ipv6=1) it installs no ::/0 in table 52 while wlan0 may have global v6, so v6 traffic bypasses the exit node. Check `ip -6 route show table 52 | grep default`. Optional hardening, exit-node-conditional ONLY (needs the bus-prefs trigger): `ip -6 route replace unreachable default table 52 metric 60000` while ExitNodeID is set; never unconditional — it would blackhole v6 for every app when no exit node is selected.

Stale 5210-5270 rules from an OLD core after a live upgrade: '5270: from all lookup 52' would swallow the new daemon's marked packets (loop) as soon as table 52 has a default. Both the daemon (delIPRules purge at Up) and the app (purge loop) remove them, and a reboot clears them (netd flushes rules); still, ship app and core together or gate on coreVersion.

If the `ip` binary drops the fwmark mask, a bare 'fwmark 0x0' rule has kernel mask 0 and matches every packet including the daemon's (loop). The verify step deletes such a rule and logs a marker; Android's iproute2 prints the mask, toybox/busybox variants must be checked (verify 1-2).

SO_MARK refused (unusual root solution / SELinux setopt denial): the probe logs 'SO_MARK ... unavailable' and UseSocketMark()=false; with the pref-200 rule present an exit node would loop. Check the log line and the mangle counter (verify 3) before relying on exit nodes; consider having the app skip the pref-200 rule (or warn) when the daemon log lacks the OK line.

Behaviour change even without an exit node: all unmarked local traffic consults table 52 before netd. Table 52 only holds tailnet /32s, 100.100.100.100/32 and accepted subnet routes, so the visible difference is that --accept-routes subnets now work in Root Mode (they never did through the 1099 /10 blanket).

Tethered/hotspot clients bypass the exit node ('iif lo' scope; netd's tethering rules handle them) — identical to Android VpnService semantics. Without 'iif lo' they would enter tailscale0 un-NATed and be dropped by the exit node.

System-permission traffic (NetworkStack validation probes, netd's DoT) now rides the exit node because netd never sets bit 25. If the exit node is down Android may flag Wi-Fi as 'no internet' or prefer cellular — expected exit-node-down behaviour, but unlike an Android VPN where probes are protectedFromVpn.

The daemon's TCP/DoH DNS fallbacks (SystemDial, forwarder.go:994) are marked and bypass the exit node; UDP fallbacks (unmarked) ride it. Same split as upstream Linux; a minor DNS-metadata leak for TCP/DoH only.

Running Root TUN and the VpnService TUN simultaneously (MainActivity.kt:441-443 starts TunVpnService when isTunModeEnabled): netd's VPN uid-range rules also capture the daemon's marked traffic (bit 17 protectedFromVpn is not set) -> blackout. Keep the two modes mutually exclusive in the UI.

netd restart flushes all rules (100 and 200): tailnet and exit-node routing silently stop until the app re-applies; today rootRoutingApplied is only reset on stop, hence the per-tick presence check recommendation.

Exit node without allow-lan-access routes LAN prefixes into tailscale0 (upstream semantics, local.go:6575-6579): Chromecast/mDNS/LAN printers stop working until LAN access is enabled (throw routes). With LAN access, LocalRoutes come from patch 06's interface getter via the anet fallback (TS_NET_STATE is only set for the appctr child, daemon.go) — confirm the 'allowing exit node access to local IPs' log lists real prefixes.
Peers whose physical endpoint is a carrier-CGNAT 100.64/10 address still hit the app's pref-100 'to 100.64.0.0/10' rule even when marked (pre-existing, unchanged).
WSA-specific: its netd rule set and table numbering may differ from a phone; read verify step 0/2 output before trusting the ordering, and note WSA often has no global IPv6.

DNS with an exit node that cannot proxy DNS (DefaultResolvers:[]) depends entirely on TS_DNS_FALLBACK (patch 11); an empty value SERVFAILs every external name. Keep it mandatory in Root Mode and keep the TAILSOCKS_DNS RETURN list in sync with it.

issues.where: app_changes / risks #5 (pref-200 install gating) — RootUtils.applyTailscale0Routing, tailscaled.sh
issues.problem: The pref-200 catch-all is installed unconditionally, but it is only safe when the running daemon actually marks its sockets. With an old core (still adds '5270: from all lookup 52', sockets unmarked) or a core whose SO_MARK probe failed, the rule turns 'exit node inert' into a device-wide routing loop the moment table 52 gets 'default dev tailscale0' (WireGuard/DERP packets to the exit node's endpoint are routed into tailscale0). The design leaves the gate as 'consider'/'ship together'.
issues.evidence: netns_android.go:25-28 (today UseSocketMark()==false, controlC :72-108 sets no mark); router_linux.go:1594-1628 + 1659-1691 (old core installs 5270 'from all lookup 52' with no mark filter); the design's own release-coupling paragraph. Failure mode asymmetry: without pref-200 and with the new core, table 52 is simply never consulted (tailnet still works via 1099); with pref-200 and unmarked sockets every exit-node activation loops.
issues.fix: Make the gate mandatory, not optional: in the app, install the pref-200 lines only after `grep -q 'netns: SO_MARK .* set on tailscaled sockets' <rootDaemonLogFile>` succeeds for the current daemon start (the daemon log is root-owned 0644, readable — RootUtils.kt:249-253), and log a WARN 'exit node unavailable: daemon does not mark sockets' otherwise. In tailscaled.sh, wait for the same line (bounded loop) before adding pref 200. Additionally have the daemon print an easily greppable single token (e.g. 'tailsocks-bypass-mark=ok').

issues.where: rules_v4 item 2 / rules_v6 item 2 (catch-all mask), verification step 2 grep patterns, RootUtils BYPASS_MARK usage
issues.problem: Mask 0x2000000 only exempts the daemon. Every other locally generated packet is routed into table 52 regardless of netd's own bypass flags, so traffic Android deliberately keeps off VPNs — sockets with protectedFromVpn (bit 17, 0x20000: NetworkStack validation probes, MmsService/phone-uid network-bound sockets, other VPN apps' protected sockets, AP-side IMS on some vendors) — is hijacked by the exit node. On the Redmi this can break MMS/carrier-provisioning and mis-validate Wi-Fi while the exit node is on; the design lists only the probe case (risk #8).
issues.evidence: Task statement's Fwmark layout (explicit 0x10000, protectedFromVpn 0x20000, permission 0xC0000); netd's own VPN rules use exactly the 'fwmark 0x0/0x20000' idiom to skip protected sockets; the design rule has no such bit in its mask. A fib rule matches when ((rule.mark ^ skb.mark) & mask)==0, so adding bit 17 to the mask makes any protected socket skip table 52 while unprotected app sockets still match.
issues.fix: Use `fwmark 0x0/0x2020000 iif lo lookup 52 priority 200` (both v4 and v6), update the verify grep to '0x0/0x2020000', and note in the rationale that this mirrors netd's VPN semantics. Do NOT widen to the permission bits 0xC0000: PERMISSION_NETWORK (0x40000) is granted to ordinary apps holding CHANGE_NETWORK_STATE and a single rule cannot express 'both permission bits set'. Keep the daemon's SO_MARK at 0x2000000 (bit 25) unchanged.

issues.problem: The original rp_filter value is saved to /data/adb/tailsocks/rp_filter.orig, but that directory is only created by RootUtils.startRootDaemon through su; on the boot-script path (tailscaled.sh) or after the directory was removed the redirect fails silently, 'echo 2 > .../all/rp_filter' still runs, and cleanup can never restore the original.
issues.evidence: RootUtils.kt:216-224 (`mkdir -p /data/adb/tailsocks && chmod 700` only in startRootDaemon); tailscaled.sh never creates it (lines 59-77 only read control_proxy.env from it); the design's item 4 has no mkdir.
issues.fix: Prefix the rp_filter step with `mkdir -p /data/adb/tailsocks && chmod 700 /data/adb/tailsocks` in both RootUtils and tailscaled.sh; also write the .orig only via a temp+mv so a partial write cannot leave a bad value.

issues.problem: On a device with IPv6 disabled (WSA frequently has no v6 rules support or disable_ipv6=1) `ip -6 rule add` fails (tolerated by `|| true`), and the verify line then prints 'verify: v6 exit-node catch-all NOT installed' on every apply; the app's proposed WARN surfacing of the marker string ('catch-all NOT installed') would raise a false alarm every time.
issues.evidence: rules_v6 items 2-3 as written; app_changes says any output containing 'catch-all NOT installed' triggers rootLog WARN.
issues.fix: Gate the v6 block on `[ -d /proc/sys/net/ipv6 ] && [ "$(cat /proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/all/disable_ipv6)" = 0 ]`, and use distinct marker strings for v4 (WARN) and v6 (INFO).

The conclusion (keep the android file, add SO_MARK there) still stands for other reasons.

If the nodeattr is ever enabled, LocalRoutes destinations would switch to SystemDial and become marked (bypassing table 52) — which is still correct because those prefixes are 'throw' anyway.

issues.problem: `ip rule del pref N` deletes the first rule at that priority regardless of its content, so the purge would also remove a third-party rule that happens to sit at 5210-5270 (unlikely but possible for another wg/VPN tool).
issues.evidence: The daemon's own delIPRules (router_linux.go:1736-1771) is deliberately more specific: it matches priority AND table/type (Mark/Mask -1).

issues.problem: Pre-existing but worth surfacing while touching this code: netd numbers per-network routing tables as 1000+ifindex, so any interface that ever gets ifindex 99 makes netd own table 1099 (netd flushes/populates it as that network comes and goes). On a phone that creates/destroys rmnet/tun/p2p/clat interfaces over long uptimes ifindex 99 is reachable. Table 52 is safe (netd uses 97-99 and >=1001 only).
issues.evidence: Task statement describes netd's per-interface tables as ifindex+1000; RootUtils.kt:20 and tailscaled.sh:116-136 hard-code 1099.
issues.fix: Out of scope for this fix, but note it as a follow-up: move the app table to a number netd cannot reach (e.g. 100-899), keeping the cleanup of 1099 for upgrades.

issues.problem: Three consequences are not listed: (a) every unmarked helper process now rides the exit node — including a configured control proxy (ByeDPI at 127.0.0.1 is loopback, but ByeDPI's own upstream sockets are unmarked), so control-plane reachability depends on the exit node whenever one is active (the user can still disable it locally over the unix LocalAPI socket); (b) IPv4 multicast/broadcast (mDNS 224.0.0.251, SSDP) from apps that do not set IP_MULTICAST_IF/oif is routed into tailscale0 even with LAN access on, because throw routes only cover unicast LAN prefixes (upstream Linux parity; apps that bind to the Wi-Fi interface are unaffected because an oif mismatch makes the table-52 lookup return -EAGAIN and fall through); (c) forcing netfilter off on Android permanently rules out this device acting as an exit node/subnet router in Root Mode (no SNAT/stateful rules) — already broken today, but now by design.
issues.evidence: tsdial.go:610-616 (user dials via stdDialer), RootUtils.kt:195-209 (HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY for control); router_linux.go:1809-1849 (SNAT/stateful gated on netfilterMode) plus platformCanNetfilter gate; kernel fib rule/oif semantics.

critique.notes:
Verified against the tree (tailscale_src = v1.102.1 + patches): the mechanism is sound and the citations check out.

Bypass claim (the crux) holds: in Root TUN mode netns stays enabled (cmd/tailscaled/tailscaled.go:815 `netns.SetEnabled(!onlyNetstack)`), so the Control hook returned by netns_android.go:64-66 is attached by netns.Listener/NewDialer/FromDialer (net/netns/netns.go:88-131) to magicsock UDP (magicsock.go:3712, 4082), DERP (derphttp_client.go:612, 714), the control plane via tsdial.SystemDial (tsdial.go:538-541), netcheck (netcheck.go:895, 1201), dnsfallback (dnsfallback.go:136) and portmapper (portmapper.go:387, upnp.go:447). Today controlC only calls the JNI hooks, which nothing in this tree registers (SetAndroidProtectFunc/SetAndroidBindToNetworkFunc have no callers outside netns), so all daemon sockets are mark 0 — the design's diagnosis that Android never marks is correct. Adding SO_MARK there is the right place; x/sys/unix builds for GOOS=android.

Kernel semantics as claimed: FRA_FWMARK=0 + FRA_FWMASK=0x2000000 gives mark_mask 0x2000000 (kernel only defaults the mask to 0xFFFFFFFF when the mark value is non-zero), match is ((rule.mark ^ skb.mark) & mask)==0; iif lo matches output lookups because ip_route_output_key/ip6_route_output set flowi_iif=LOOPBACK_IFINDEX (the same idiom netd uses at 22000/16000); rp_filter's reverse lookup runs with iif lo and mark 0 (no src_valid_mark), so strict mode would drop replies and loose mode passes them after the oif-constrained second lookup — the design's rp_filter step is necessary and sufficient (effective value is max(all, iface)). netd's default rule 'fwmark 0x0/0xffff' still matches 0x2000000 (low 16 bits zero). RTN_THROW returns -EAGAIN to the rule walker so LAN throws fall through to netd as described.

Router gates: platformCanNetfilter() is the single choke point (router_linux.go:746-748 forces mode Off; :1944 skips cleanUp's netfilter). With mode Off every nfr.* call is gated: connmark (:555-586 keyed on r.netfilterMode==On and connmarkEnabled, both false → no-op), CGNAT (:596-597), magicsock port (:716), loopback (:1158, :1174), SNAT/stateful (:1809-1849). Only Close() :396 DelConnmarkSaveRule runs unconditionally and is log-only. linuxfw.New → newNfTablesRunner → nftables.New() is lazy (non-lasting conn, no socket until first op) and CheckIPv6 (linuxfw.go:122-162) is /proc + netlink RuleList, so HasIPV6()/getV6Available keep working and v6 addresses/routes are still installed on a kernel with no nf_tables at all (relevant for GKI phones). Set() collects errors and still programs routes (:444-475), and SetRouterHealth(nil) clears the 'router' warning (userspace.go:893-901). Forcing ipRuleAvailable=true makes routeTable() return 52 (:1375-1380) and enables throw routes (:1213-1215); with ipRules() returning nil on android, addIPRules → delIPRules(baseIPRules) → justAddIPRules is a pure purge; onIPRuleDeleted only watches 5200-5299 so the app must own re-adding pref 100/200 after a netd restart (the per-tick presence check in the design is needed). Tailscale's own marks 0x40000/0x80000/0xff0000 (tsconst/linuxfw.go:31-42) are indeed netd's permission bits 18-19 — another reason never to run upstream netfilter on Android.

Build/patch plumbing: build.sh applies with -F0 and fails on empty patches (:60-70); recreate_patches.sh already diffs router_linux.go into patch 13 and has the empty-patch guard, so a new 16-android-somark.patch line is the right approach. TS_DEBUG_FIREWALL_MODE=iptables on this binary would fail hard (iptables_disabled.go:14-19 → setupNetfilterLocked error → Up fails → userspace.go:557-559). OverrideDNSResolvers is dead: localapi.go:1010-1011 decodes into ipn.MaskedPrefs with a plain json.Decoder that ignores unknown fields.

Ordering with the existing app rules: pref 100 'to 100.64.0.0/10' and the fwmark-bit-24 rule win before 200, so tailnet destinations and the DNAT'd 100.100.100.100 path are unchanged; the DNS forwarder's UDP upstream socket is unmarked (forwarder.go:504-512) and will ride the exit node, TCP/DoH fallbacks use SystemDial (forwarder.go:991-994) and bypass it. Exit-node removal is a plain RouteDel in table 52; a killed daemon leaves only device-less throw routes behind (a new router starts with empty localRoutes so stale throws persist until Close) — minor. Toybox concern: Android's /system/bin/ip is iproute2, all syntax used (pref/priority, fwmark a/b, iif, lookup, 'route get ... mark') is valid; the mask-verify step correctly handles a hypothetical busybox ip.

The observed WSA state ('table 52 empty, no 52xx rules') is consistent with hypothesis (b): if netlink.RuleList had succeeded, Up() would have added 5210-5270 or exited; so on WSA ipRuleAvailable was most likely false and the exit-node default landed in RT_TABLE_MAIN, which no netd rule consults (netd's flushRules removes 32766/32767). The 'sites not loading' symptom is then most plausibly DNS (DefaultResolvers=[] → TS_DNS_FALLBACK only) rather than a loop; step 0 of the verification will settle it and gate 4 fixes both cases by construction.

Verdict rationale: no flaw in the routing/marking design was found; the blocking item is procedural (the pref-200 rule must be conditioned on proof that the daemon marks sockets, since the opposite failure mode is a device-wide loop), and the protectedFromVpn mask change is a cheap fidelity improvement that avoids hijacking MMS/IMS/system probes.
